name: reject-tampered-resourcejwt
description: An unlock request an issuer must refuse whole: a genuine resourceJWT whose payload was edited after signing. THE ATTACK. The token's header and signature segments are the publisher's own, byte for byte the ones in seal-ecdh.json from the same run. Between them, date.published in the payload was moved from "2025-10-20T10:30:00Z" to "2025-10-23T13:59:00Z" - one minute before the pinned clock. The renderId is untouched, so every blob in the body would open if the request got that far: what the edit buys, on an issuer that does not verify over the edited bytes, is an access decision made on the attacker's claims - a metered policy that grants by article age reads a three-day-old article as published a minute ago. WHY IT IS REFUSED. ES256 verifies over the exact bytes of "<header>.<payload>". The signature was drawn over the original payload and does not verify over this one, and there is no field-level integrity to appeal to: one edited byte anywhere in the payload is this same refusal. THE FAMILY. reject-forged-resourcejwt is the wrong key over the right bytes; this is the right key over the wrong bytes; reject-alg-substituted and its HS256 arm are neither, because the header there names a different check and the ECDSA verify these two fail is never run at all. The three are the negative space of the one signature check on the wire: an issuer that pins the key and pins the bytes but reads the algorithm off the header refuses this vector and its forged sibling, and hands the whole render to the third. This tamper changes the only resource representation on the wire, so editing the signed copy kills the whole request. A CONFORMANT ISSUER answers 400 with bad_signature and no key of any kind, before its private key is touched: one verification spent, zero ECDH operations. expected.privateKeyReached is false. REPLAY. Post `rawBody` VERBATIM - the string as it sits in this file, never a re-serialization of it - to the unlock endpoint, with `issuer` as the key material the issuer holds for its own name and keyId, and `publisher.signingKeys` as the public verification halves, read straight from this file rather than resolved by a deployment lookup. A pass is: expected.code where there is one; key material back for exactly the coordinates in expected.keys and no others; and an error back for exactly the coordinates in expected.errors, under the codes recorded there. No publisher private key is in this file, on purpose: an issuer never holds one, so everything a reject vector asks for is checkable with what a real issuer has. HOW FAR THE REFUSAL REACHES IS PART OF WHAT IS PINNED, and expected.privateKeyReached says which side of the line this body lands on. A request that fails integrity - a signature that does not verify, a signed resource with no renderId to bind to - has asked nothing that could be answered, so it is refused whole and before the key store is consulted at all. A blob presented at a coordinate it was not sealed at is one bad blob in an ordinary request: the only way to find out is to try it, so the key store is reached, the blob comes back as an error, and everything else the request carried is answered beside it. The untouched coordinates were never the attack, and a page has to keep working around one bad blob, so they are answered. Everything in the body but the attack is the render this vector was cut from - the envelope, the periodKeys section and the untouched blobs are what the publisher emitted. An unchanged regeneration retains the valid resourceJWT signature segment inside rawBody, so the body is byte-stable with seal-ecdh.json. A fresh seal still draws a new k, which is why a replayer verifies the segment rather than comparing it. The token is the one in the base vector from the same run, byte for byte, except in reject-no-renderid, reject-renderid-noncanonical and reject-renderid-wrong-width, whose envelopes are second tokens signed over resources with the renderId removed, given a noncanonical spelling, or resized, which is each vector's whole subject; in reject-forged-resourcejwt, whose signature segment was drawn by a key the publisher does not hold; in reject-tampered-resourcejwt, which carries the seal-ecdh token's own signature segment under a payload edited after signing; and in the two reject-alg-substituted arms, which carry that token's payload segment under a header rewritten to name another algorithm, with a third segment that is empty or a MAC - neither of which moves between runs.
